title: Ship a reviewed change with confidence
goal: You will review your branch diff for bugs, obtain a concise summary, apply a verified fix, and inspect the final changes before pushing.
prerequisites: Claude Code is installed and authenticated
Your repository has a configured remote
Your project’s test command works locally

steps.action: Open a terminal at the repository root and run `git status --short --branch`.
steps.where: Terminal window at the repository’s top-level directory.
steps.why: This confirms the active branch and reveals uncommitted files before the review begins.
steps.checkpoint: The first line shows your branch, followed by any modified or untracked files.
hint_levels: Check your branch before involving Claude.
Use Git’s short status view from the folder containing `.git`.
In the terminal, type `git status --short --branch` and press Enter.

steps.action: Run `git fetch origin` to refresh the remote comparison point.
steps.where: Same terminal prompt at the repository root.
steps.why: A current remote reference prevents Claude from reviewing against stale branch data.
steps.checkpoint: The command finishes without an authentication or repository error.
hint_levels: Refresh the remote references without changing your files.
Fetch from the remote normally named `origin`.
Type `git fetch origin` and press Enter.

steps.where: Same terminal prompt at the repository root.
steps.why: Launching here gives Claude access to the repository and its Git history.
steps.checkpoint: The Claude Code prompt appears and identifies the current project directory.
hint_levels: Launch the coding agent from inside the repository.
The Claude Code CLI command is `claude`.
Type `claude` and press Enter, then complete any displayed trust prompt.

steps.action: Ask Claude to review the complete branch diff against its merge base without editing files.
steps.where: Claude Code conversation prompt in the terminal.
steps.why: A read-only first pass separates diagnosis from implementation.
steps.checkpoint: Claude displays findings tied to files or lines and has not proposed an edit for approval.
hint_levels: Specify the comparison branch and forbid edits for now.
Request concrete correctness bugs in committed and uncommitted changes, ranked by severity.

Enter: `Review my complete branch diff against origin/main using the merge base, including uncommitted changes. Do not edit files. Find concrete bugs, rank them by severity, and cite file paths and lines.`

steps.action: Ask Claude to summarize the diff’s purpose, affected areas, risks, and test coverage.
steps.where: Claude Code conversation prompt beneath the review response.
steps.why: A structured summary helps you understand the branch before choosing a fix.
steps.checkpoint: Claude returns a compact summary containing purpose, affected areas, risks, and tests.
hint_levels: Turn the review into a branch-level overview.
Name the four sections you want so the response stays useful.
Enter: `Summarize this branch in four sections: purpose, affected areas, key risks, and existing or missing tests.`

steps.action: Ask Claude to explain the highest-severity finding and propose the smallest safe fix.
steps.where: Claude Code conversation prompt beneath the summary.
steps.why: Validating one finding before editing reduces the chance of fixing a false positive.
steps.checkpoint: Claude explains a failure scenario and names the specific files it would change.
hint_levels: Focus on the most consequential credible issue.
Require a reproducible failure scenario and a minimal patch plan.
Enter: `For the highest-severity credible bug, explain the failure scenario and propose the smallest safe fix, including the files and tests you would change. Do not edit yet.`

steps.action: Tell Claude to implement that fix and add or update a focused regression test.
steps.where: Claude Code conversation prompt, followed by Claude Code’s edit-permission prompt if one appears.
steps.why: The regression test demonstrates the bug and protects the corrected behavior.
steps.checkpoint: Claude reports modified files, and its diff view shows both the fix and a focused test change.
hint_levels: Approve only the scoped plan you just inspected.
Ask for the minimal implementation plus a regression test, then review any permission request.
Enter: `Implement that minimal fix and add or update a focused regression test. Avoid unrelated refactoring.` Then approve only the expected file edits when prompted.

steps.action: Ask Claude to run the focused test and the project’s relevant validation command.
steps.where: Claude Code conversation prompt and any shell-command approval prompt.
steps.why: Executing validation confirms the patch works in the real project.
steps.checkpoint: The terminal shows passing results, or Claude reports a specific remaining failure with command output.
hint_levels: Validate the narrow behavior first, then the surrounding project.
Have Claude run the regression test and the repository’s established lint, typecheck, or test command.
Enter: `Run the focused regression test, then run the relevant project validation commands for these files. Report the exact commands and results.` Approve the expected non-destructive commands.

steps.action: Exit Claude Code and inspect the final patch with `git diff --check` followed by `git diff`.
steps.where: Claude Code prompt using `/exit`, then the normal terminal prompt at the repository root.
steps.why: A final human inspection catches whitespace errors and confirms only intended changes remain.
steps.checkpoint: `git diff --check` prints no errors, and `git diff` shows only the reviewed fix and test changes.
hint_levels: Finish with Git’s own view of the working tree.
Leave Claude, check patch formatting, and then read the complete diff.
Enter `/exit`, then run `git diff --check`; if it is clean, run `git diff` and inspect every changed hunk.
